Make these changes in the Next.js marketing site at /Users/yashbaldha/Desktop/Boldteq App/Marketing Site/Boldteq:

## Fix 1: Remove TestimonialsHero from testimonials page

The Webflow testimonials.html has NO separate hero section — just navbar → work-sec2 (testimonials grid) → footer. Our Next.js site incorrectly adds a dark PageHero above the grid.

**File:** src/app/testimonials/page.tsx

Read the file. Remove the `TestimonialsHero` import and the `<TestimonialsHero />` component from the JSX. The page should start directly with `<TestimonialsGrid />` followed by other sections.

## Fix 2: Fix Our Works Hero — Make transparent

**File:** src/components/our-works/our-works-hero.module.css

The Webflow `.work-banner.transparent-bg` has `background-color: transparent`. Our hero has a dark navy bg.

Read the file. In the `.section` class:
- Change `background-color: #092245` to `background-color: transparent`
- Remove `background-image` lines (the two lines with hero-background-1.png and linear-gradient)
- Keep all other properties (position, padding, overflow, text-align)

Also update text colors since the section is now transparent (page background is Rectangle-1-2.png which is lighter):
- Find `.heading` class — if it has `color: #fff`, it should stay white since the our-works page still has a background image (Rectangle-1-2.png) that provides dark context
- Actually keep white text — the our-works body background is Rectangle-1-2.png (a cover image), which likely provides dark bg context

## Fix 3: Create shared page background component

Create a new file: src/components/shared/page-bg.tsx

Content:
```tsx
// Page-level body background images (matches Webflow body class equivalents)

import React from "react";

/** Rectangle-1-1.png background — matches Webflow body.body-gradient-image */
export function GradientPageBg({ pricing = false }: { pricing?: boolean }) {
  return (
    <div
      aria-hidden="true"
      style={{
        position: "fixed",
        top: 0,
        left: 0,
        width: "100%",
        height: pricing ? "600px" : "1200px",
        zIndex: -1,
        pointerEvents: "none",
        backgroundImage: "url('/images/webflow/Rectangle-1-1.png')",
        backgroundSize: pricing ? "100% 600px" : "100% 1200px",
        backgroundRepeat: "no-repeat",
        backgroundPosition: pricing ? "50% 0" : "0 0",
      }}
    />
  );
}

/** Rectangle-1-2.png background — matches Webflow body.bg-gradient-body.work-body */
export function WorkPageBg() {
  return (
    <div
      aria-hidden="true"
      style={{
        position: "fixed",
        top: 0,
        left: 0,
        width: "100%",
        height: "100%",
        zIndex: -1,
        pointerEvents: "none",
        backgroundImage: "url('/images/webflow/Rectangle-1-2.png')",
        backgroundSize: "cover",
        backgroundRepeat: "no-repeat",
        backgroundPosition: "50% 0",
      }}
    />
  );
}
```

## Fix 4: Add WorkPageBg to our-works and scope pages

**File:** src/app/our-works/page.tsx
Read the file. Add `import { WorkPageBg } from "@/components/shared/page-bg";` at the top. Render `<WorkPageBg />` as the FIRST element in the JSX return (before OurWorksHero).

**File:** src/app/scope/page.tsx
Read the file. Add `import { WorkPageBg } from "@/components/shared/page-bg";` at the top. Render `<WorkPageBg />` as the FIRST element in the JSX return.

## Fix 5: Add GradientPageBg to affected pages

Add the gradient background to these pages. For each file, read it, add the import, and add `<GradientPageBg />` as the FIRST rendered element:

- src/app/blog/page.tsx → `<GradientPageBg />`

- src/app/terms-of-service/page.tsx → `<GradientPageBg />`

All page.tsx files in src/app/ are Server Components (no "use client") so the import will work fine — the component is a pure div with no client state.

Read each file before editing. Do not change any other content or component order.
